changes.before: Label completed chapter progress and a bounded notebook-space meter with the displayed values.
changes.after: Show work completed separately from space used.

before: Prerequisite: explicit labels. progress represents task completion: value is work completed and max is the positive total. Omitting value means indeterminate progress, not zero completion. meter instead describes a scalar measurement within a known range, such as percentage of storage used.

For meter, min/max bound the range, low/high divide it into regions, and optimum identifies a preferred value. Here 10 is in the low region, while 90 is above high=80: greater storage use is less desirable. Styling and color are browser-dependent; keep meaningful labels and text rather than relying on color.

```html
<label for="done">Chapters reviewed</label>
<progress id="done" value="3" max="8">3 of 8</progress>
<label for="space">Notebook space used</label>
<meter id="space" min="0" max="100" low="20" high="80" optimum="10" value="90">90 percent</meter>
```

```html
<label for="done">Chapters reviewed</label>
<progress id="done" max="8">3 of 8</progress>
<label for="space">Notebook space used</label>
<meter id="space" min="0" max="100" low="20" high="80" optimum="10" value="90">90 percent</meter>
```
No value means indeterminate progress. It does not assert that zero of eight chapters have been reviewed. The changed snapshot deliberately retains stale fallback text (3 of 8); a real UI must also update that text to an honest unknown-progress message.
Optional: change one relevant value, predict the effect, and compare the parsed attributes. Structural checks do not prove browser presentation or accessibility.
after:
`<progress>` shows how much of a task is done.

```html
<label for="done">Chapters reviewed</label>
<progress id="done" value="3" max="8">3 of 8</progress>
```

`value="3"` means three chapters are done. `max="8"` is the total. The label tells us what is being counted.
If you leave out progress’s `value`, the amount done is unknown. That is different from zero. Update any matching text to say the progress is unknown too, so it does not claim an exact amount.

`<meter>` shows a measurement within a range, rather than task completion.

```html
<label for="space">Notebook space used</label>
<meter id="space" min="0" max="100" low="20" high="80" optimum="10" value="90">90 percent</meter>
```

The range goes from 0 to 100. `value="90"` means 90 percent of the notebook space is used. The label tells us what is measured.

In this meter, low and high mark the range’s lower and upper regions. `optimum="10"` marks a preferred value near the low end: using less space is better here. The current value, 90, is above high=80. Browser colors can differ, so keep clear words as well.

Add the two labeled elements from the examples. Progress should show 3 of 8 chapters. The meter should show 90 within 0 to 100, with low 20, high 80 and optimum 10. Use ids `done` and `space` to match their labels, then run the checks.
